subject: RShiny Crashes when i try to switch between SQL Database Server

messages.author: 2d1220ee6c3a3d48
messages.subject: RShiny Crashes when i try to switch between SQL Database Server
parts:
Hello All,

I'm trying to make a visualization tool wherein the data's are stored in two different Database but in same Database server.

Everything works fine i.e. i'm able to plot the maps spatially and visualize it,if i select the first database and also after that if wish to select the 2nd database,i'm also able to do it.But the problem occurs if i try to again select the First database ,Shiny Crashes.

#Snippet of Code 

shinyServer(function(input, output,session){
  
  #' Get list of Databases at that particular server 
  output$database <- renderUI({
    dbhandl <- odbcDriverConnect('driver={SQL Server};server={Name of Server};trusted_connection=true')
    list_tables <- sqlQuery(dbhandl, "SELECT name FROM master..sysdatabases WHERE name LIKE 'NAME_%'")
    selectizeInput("ser",strong('Select Database:'),choices = list_tables[,1],selected = NULL,multiple = FALSE)
  })
  
  #' Create SQL connection with that particular server and particular Database server name
  db_connect <- reactive({
    if(input$ser =={Name of Database 1}){
      dbhandle <- odbcDriverConnect("driver={SQL Server};server={Name of Server};database={Name of Database 1};trusted_connection=true")
    }else if(input$ser == {Name of Database 2}){
      dbhandle <- odbcDriverConnect("driver={SQL Server};server={Name of Server};database={Name of Database 2};trusted_connection=true")
    }
  })
   
and there are whole lot of other reactive elements after this which generally extracts table from SQL query and which is further need to plot the map.

It would be really nice if some one can help me through this.

Thanks in advance

messages.author: d6ebe55625e8e5a2
messages.subject: Re: RShiny Crashes when i try to switch between SQL Database Server
parts:
Without a runnable MRE, it's hard to tell the particular reason why your app is failing. What I can tell you, however, is that you should never be opening connections inside reactive blocks and not closing them -- it's possible that's what is causing the crash. On the other hand, it seems like you are using the RODBC package, which has some known issues.. Have you looked into the recent odbc package? I think you'd be much better off with that. It's also DBI compliant, which means that in addition to having access to the very well maintained DBI interface, you can also use the dplyr and pool packages to create robust code that interacts efficiently with databases. The dplyr package translates dplyr code to SQL to allow you to query a database in a friendlier language and the pool package does connection management for you (i.e. if you follow best practices, you won't have to worry about closing connections, which is a likely cause for the problem you're experiencing now). If your app is large, this may mean that you have to invest some time upfront to migrate everything, but I'd strongly advice you to do that anyway.

If this sounds interesting to you, in addition to the link above, you should check out the following three articles (in this order):
  1. Database basics - dplyr and DBI
  2. Using the pool package (basics)
  3. Using dplyr and pool to query a database
